title: Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Amendment (Restoring Merits Review) Bill 2014
short_title: Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Amendment (Restoring Merits Review) Bill 2014

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would give asylum seekers access to the Administrative Appeals Tribunal to challenge adverse security assessments by the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation.
It would remove migration-related exclusions from security assessment review procedures and prevent asylum seeker status from restricting matters considered by the tribunal.
It would also enable review when new information emerges, with the amendments commencing on the day after the bill receives Royal Assent.
changes: Migration action would be removed from the definition of prescribed administrative action.
The exclusion that denies some migration cases the usual security assessment procedures would be repealed.
Regulations could not use asylum seeker status to prescribe matters for tribunal consideration.
Restrictions on reviewing migration security assessments when new information becomes available would be removed.
summary.affected: Asylum seekers subject to adverse security assessments and the Administrative Appeals Tribunal would be affected.
